Twelve days ago, I placed an order through their website, and after eleven days, I still hadn't received any information whatsoever about its status.
Following a review I posted expressing my dissatisfaction with this situation, I received a phone call from the owner. Unfortunately, the way she spoke to me was far from what I consider professional and respectful service: an arrogant and overbearing tone, constant interruptions, shouting, and an attitude that didn't allow me to calmly explain the reason for my complaint.
During the call, I was told that they work by hand in a small workshop. Up to that point, I have absolutely no objection. I perfectly understand that a small, artisanal business might need more time to prepare and ship its products. That's not the issue.

The problem is that the product was listed as "in stock" on the website when, apparently, it wasn't, and that the order was subsequently delayed for eleven days without me receiving any clear communication about it. If a product is listed as in stock, it's reasonable to assume that units are available for shipment. If this isn't the case due to a website error, I believe the least professional course of action would have been to inform the customer of the error and explain that their order would be delayed.

What's particularly contradictory is that, as I was told during the call, emails and text messages had been sent informing me of the situation, and that I should check my spam folder or that they might have been sent to the wrong email address. At that time, I naturally thought it could be a misunderstanding and accepted that possibility.

However, I later thoroughly checked my email, including my spam folder, as well as my text messages, and there is absolutely no trace of any communication from them related to the delay or the supposed stock error.

Therefore, my complaint was very simple: I don't question that it's a small, artisanal business, nor that they might need more time to prepare an order. What I question is that a product appears as available when it isn't, that the order remains unread for days, and that the customer only finds out about the situation after publicly expressing their dissatisfaction.

I believe that an issue like this can be easily resolved with clear communication, an apology, and an explanation. What I find unacceptable is receiving a call in which, instead of trying to solve the problem, I'm spoken to in a raised voice, constantly interrupted, and not allowed to express my point of view.
A bad experience with an order can be understandable; a lack of communication can also be due to a mistake. What I find unjustifiable is the way the complaint was handled and, especially, the treatment I received from the owner.

A deeply disappointing experience.

I booked an appointment to have my puppy's hair cut. During the call, I explained that I wanted a natural cut and was told that I would discuss the details with the groomer on the day of the appointment. However, upon arrival, I was informed that the schedule only showed a bath with a minor trim.

My dog ​​had been bathed two days prior, and since the full service required two hours and the appointment was only an hour and a half, I proposed a common-sense solution: skip the bath and dedicate that time to the haircut, even if the full service charge was applied. The response was negative.

The initial mistake is understandable. The complete lack of flexibility in resolving it is not. I wasted the trip, the time invested, and had to reschedule two professional meetings for nothing.

Premium prices are only justified by premium service. In my experience, the gap between the two was significant.
